text: The actions of a new prince are more narrowly observed than those of an hereditary one, and when they are seen to be able they gain more men and bind far tighter than ancient blood; because men are attracted more by the present than by the past, and when they find the present good they enjoy it and seek no further.
author: Niccolo Machiavelli
locator: Chapter XXIV, Why the princes of Italy have lost their states
location: Sant'Andrea in Percussina, near Florence, Italy
